pr_comments:
For what it's worth, an opinion on the change. 

This does not address the core of the issue, the fact is the previous change have broken a public API promise. With this proposed change implementations that override the protected methods are still broken. Provided they relied on previous behaviour where `getUnadjustedFrameLength` was called multiple times. The only way to fix this is to revert the change.

Now if you want to expose some new API, e.g. something an implementor of the `getUnadjustedFrameLength` can call to signal that there will be no more changes to the provided frame length that is fine. You can then go ahed and update any existing implementation that need the optimisation.

E.g. instead of `public void resetFrameLengthInt()` have a `public void memoizeFrameLength()` after calling that no more calls to the `getUnadjustedFrameLength` will be made. The last emitted value would stand.

Further, more if you do want to keep this change, go ahead and use the new API e.g. line:445 in the current implementation should really use it as well.

issue_context.title: LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder Class Can be optimized
issue_context.body:
### Expected behavior
LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder . decode(ChannelHandlerContext ctx, ByteBuf in) method，Can be optimized - Can we keep frameLengthInt in instance variable? so , When there is not enough data in the buffer, the length of the data frame does not need to be recalculated at the next decoding。code:

// LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder class 
protected Object decode(ChannelHandlerContext ctx, ByteBuf in) throws Exception {
        ... // check maxFrame 
        int frameLengthInt = (int) frameLength;
        if (in.readableBytes() < frameLengthInt) {  **//  When there is not enough data in the buffer, The above code will be executed again, and I just need to wait for the buffer to contain enough data . In fact, we can save the frameLengthInt variable without having to**  
            return null;
        }
        ... // extract frame
    }
### Actual behavior
When there is not enough data in the buffer, the length of the data frame  recalculate at the next decoding

comments:
First off, thanks for making and maintaining Netty. Don't take it as a complaint but as a heads up.

This is a braking change. It regresses expected behaviour of the LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder.

The `protected long getUnadjustedFrameLength(ByteBuf buf, int offset, int length, ByteOrder order)` is marked `protected` it is deemed a point of extension and therefore is a part of the public API. Nothing in the documentation of the method states what behaviour should be expected by the implementors i.e. whether it  is expected to be called once or multiple times. However, prior to the change it was invoked multiple time. As such it is now (was) part of the expected, albeit undocumented, behaviour. 

I have an ASN1 frame decoder, that broker after a recent upgrade that I traced to this change.  ASN1 allows frames of be variable length, the length field itself is variable width. Prior to the change, if the buffer contained partial frame that truncated the length filed, it was possible to first return a frame length that would ensure enough bytes were read to decode the length header. With a subsequent call to the `getUnadjustedFrameLength` decoding a full frame length. I.e. it was possible to progressively decode the length of the frame. After the change this is no-longer possible.

Not a show stopper, but I can no-longer use provided LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder.

Cheers!
